Cairo-Egypt.name: Cairo
Cairo-Egypt.evidence_basis: Jomard in Description de l'Egypte (~263k in 1800), 1846-48 Muhammad Ali census (Alleaume & Fargues 253,541 after 1835 plague), official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (374,838 to 2,090,654), and Abu-Lughod (1971) Cairo.

Alexandria-Egypt.name: Alexandria
Alexandria-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte (~12k in 1800), Mahmudiyah Canal revival (1820) and Clot-Bey/Reimer Colonial Bridgehead (1846 census 104,128), and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (231,396 to 919,024).

Port Said-Egypt.name: Port Said
Port Said-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded April 1859 at northern Suez Canal terminus; Suez Canal Company worker rosters (1865) and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (16,560 to 177,703).

Tanta-Egypt.name: Tanta
Tanta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte (~10.5k permanent town around Sayyid al-Badawi shrine), 1846 Gharbiya registers, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (33,750 to 139,926; central Delta railway and cotton hub).

El-Mahalla el-Kubra-Egypt.name: El-Mahalla el-Kubra
El-Mahalla el-Kubra-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte textile town estimate, official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (27,851 to 115,758), reflecting explosive post-1927 industrialization around the Bank Misr Spinning and Weaving mills.

Suez-Egypt.name: Suez
Suez-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte (~3.2k Red Sea port), Overland Mail & 1869 Canal opening revival, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (10,919 to 107,244 with WWI/WWII oil refineries and port expansion).

Mansoura-Egypt.name: Mansoura
Mansoura-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte, 1846 Dakahlia provincial registers, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (26,942 to 101,965; eastern Delta cotton-ginning capital).

Asyut-Egypt.name: Asyut
Asyut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte (Darb al-Arba'in caravan terminus ~18k), 1846 Upper Egypt census, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (31,575 to 90,103; capital of Upper Egypt).

Damanhur-Egypt.name: Damanhur
Damanhur-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte, 1846 Beheira registers, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (23,353 to 84,352; Beheira provincial capital on Cairo-Alexandria railway).

Giza-Egypt.name: Giza
Giza-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte west-bank town, 1846 census, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (11,410 to 66,156; rapid suburban integration with Cairo after 1927).

Zagazig-Egypt.name: Zagazig
Zagazig-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1832 by Muhammad Ali at Mu'izz Canal barrages as Sharqia capital; 1846 provincial count and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (19,815 to 81,813).

Faiyum-Egypt.name: Faiyum
Faiyum-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte oasis capital estimate, 1846 census, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (25,799 to 73,642; 1907 EB11 37,320).

Ismailia-Egypt.name: Ismailia
Ismailia-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1863 as Suez Canal Company administrative headquarters on Lake Timsah; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (3,364 to 68,229, boosted by British Canal Zone garrison).

Minya-Egypt.name: Minya
Minya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte, 1846 Middle Egypt census, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (15,900 to 70,298; major sugar and cotton provincial capital).

Beni Suef-Egypt.name: Beni Suef
Beni Suef-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte woollen-weaving town, 1846 census, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (10,085 to 57,106; 1907 EB11 23,357).

Shubra al-Khaymah-Egypt.name: Shubra al-Khaymah
Shubra al-Khaymah-Egypt.evidence_basis: Small Qalyubiya agrarian village north of Cairo (1800-1917 village returns) transformed by 1930s-1940s textile industrialization and WWII migration into northern industrial suburb (1937-1947 Dawahi Misr census returns; Abu-Lughod 1965).

Damietta-Egypt.name: Damietta
Damietta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte major Ottoman rice/linen port (~28k), 1846 registers, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (34,046 dipping to 29,354 in 1907 as Alexandria/Port Said took sea trade, recovering to 53,631).

Helwan-Egypt.name: Helwan
Helwan-Egypt.evidence_basis: Small village refounded as Khedive Ismail's sulfur-spring spa resort (1868-1874) with Cairo railway (1889); 1882-1947 census qism/markaz returns and pre-1952 cement/industrial growth.

Sohag-Egypt.name: Sohag
Sohag-Egypt.evidence_basis: Elevated to Girga mudiriya administrative capital in 1860s; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (8,774 to 43,168; Tanada 1997 and Abu-Lughod 1965).

Qena-Egypt.name: Qena
Qena-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte Quseir caravan/pottery hub, official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (15,402 spiking to 27,478 in 1897 during Sudan campaigns, 20,069 in 1907, 42,929 in 1947).

Shibin el-Kom-Egypt.name: Shibin el-Kom
Shibin el-Kom-Egypt.evidence_basis: Menufia provincial capital; Tanada (1997) official Egyptian censuses 1882 (16,250), 1897 (20,705), 1907 (21,576), 1917 (24,604), and 1927-1947 CAPMAS bandar returns.

Banha-Egypt.name: Banha
Banha-Egypt.evidence_basis: Qalyubiya provincial capital and major Delta railway junction (1854 Cairo-Alexandria line); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (Tanada 1997; CAPMAS 1947 ~35.9k).

Tahta-Egypt.name: Tahta
Tahta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Major Upper Egyptian grain and livestock market town in Girga/Sohag province; official censuses 1882-1947 (Abu-Lughod 1965 Table 1: 37,095 in 1947).

Mallawi-Egypt.name: Mallawi
Mallawi-Egypt.evidence_basis: Middle Egypt agricultural and cotton-trading markaz town; Tanada (1997) 1882-1917 census growth and Abu-Lughod (1965 Table 1: 35,624 in 1947).

Akhmim-Egypt.name: Akhmim
Akhmim-Egypt.evidence_basis: Historic east-bank textile-weaving town; Description de l'Egypte, 1907 census (EB11: 23,795), and 1947 census (Abu-Lughod 1965 Table 1: 34,788).

Girga-Egypt.name: Girga
Girga-Egypt.evidence_basis: Former Ottoman capital of Upper Egypt; Description de l'Egypte, 1907 census (EB11: 19,893), and 1947 census (Abu-Lughod 1965 Table 1: 33,631).

Kafr el-Dawwar-Egypt.name: Kafr el-Dawwar
Kafr el-Dawwar-Egypt.evidence_basis: Mahmudiyah Canal and railway market village (1882-1927 Beheira returns) transformed into a major industrial city by Misr Fine Spinning (1938) and Misr Rayon (1946) textile mills.

Zifta-Egypt.name: Zifta
Zifta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Damietta-branch Nile barrage and cotton-ginning town; Tanada (1997) official censuses 1882-1917 (11,087; 14,039; 15,850; 18,299) and Abu-Lughod (1965) 1947 (~31k).

Menuf-Egypt.name: Menuf
Menuf-Egypt.evidence_basis: Former capital of Menufia until 1826; Description de l'Egypte, 1907 census (EB11: 22,316), and 1947 census (Abu-Lughod 1965 Table 1: 31,475).

Mit Ghamr-Egypt.name: Mit Ghamr
Mit Ghamr-Egypt.evidence_basis: Dakahlia commercial town on east bank of Damietta branch; Tanada (1997) censuses 1882-1917 (11,375 to 17,879) and Abu-Lughod (1965 Table 1: 29,030 in 1947).

Qalyub-Egypt.name: Qalyub
Qalyub-Egypt.evidence_basis: Historic capital of Qalyubiya (until replaced by Banha) and rail junction north of Cairo; Description de l'Egypte and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Desouk-Egypt.name: Desouk
Desouk-Egypt.evidence_basis: Rosetta-branch shrine town (Ibrahim al-Desuqi) and railway hub; Tanada (1997) notes rapid 1897-1907 madina growth; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Matariya-Egypt.name: El-Matariya
El-Matariya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Lake Manzala fishing headquarters in Dakahlia; 1907 census (EB11: 15,142) and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Luxor-Egypt.name: Luxor
Luxor-Egypt.evidence_basis: Small village around ancient Thebes transformed by Thomas Cook Nile steamship tourism (1869) and railway (1898); official censuses 1897-1947 (Abu-Lughod 1965 Table 1: 27,457 in 1947, excl. rural Karnak hamlets).

Rosetta-Egypt.name: Rosetta
Rosetta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Description de l'Egypte (~15k port), eclipsed after 1820 Mahmudiyah Canal diverted trade to Alexandria; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (16,666; 1907 EB11 16,810; 1947 28,698).

Port Tawfîq-Egypt.name: Port Tawfîq
other_names: قسم أول ويتبعها بور توفيق والزيتيات والمنطقة السكنية التابعة لمعمل تكرير البترول الأميري الواقعة بالجزء الشرقي لشريط السكة الحديد

Kafr el-Sheikh-Egypt.name: Kafr el-Sheikh
Kafr el-Sheikh-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Gharbiya markaz seat (briefly renamed Fuadiya, made separate governorate capital in 1949/1955); official 1882-1947 census markaz/madina returns.

Warrâq al-Hadar wa- Ambûba wa-Mît al-Nas.name: Warrâq al-Hadar wa- Ambûba wa-Mît al-Nasârâ

Sinnuris-Egypt.name: Sinnuris
Sinnuris-Egypt.evidence_basis: Second largest town of the Faiyum depression; 1846 Faiyum registers and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (Tanada 1997; CAPMAS).

El-Fashn-Egypt.name: El-Fashn
El-Fashn-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern Beni Suef markaz capital on the Upper Egypt railway; official censuses 1882-1947 (Abu-Lughod 1965 ranks Al-Fashn among 20k-30k towns in 1947).

Faqus-Egypt.name: Faqus
Faqus-Egypt.evidence_basis: Eastern Sharqia cotton and agricultural markaz center on railway to Salhiya; Tanada (1997) and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Maghagha-Egypt.name: Maghagha
Maghagha-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Minya sugarcane and cotton rail town (Daira Saniya sugar mill built 1870s); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Ashmun-Egypt.name: Ashmun
Ashmun-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern Menufia cotton-growing markaz town near Delta Barrages; Tanada (1997) notes rapid 1897-1907 madina growth; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Manfalut-Egypt.name: Manfalut
Manfalut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Historic Asyut-province river town damaged by 19th-century Nile bank erosion; Description de l'Egypte, official censuses 1882-1947 (Tanada 1997; Abu-Lughod 1965).

Bilbays-Egypt.name: Bilbays
Bilbays-Egypt.evidence_basis: Historic eastern Delta fortress town; Tanada (1997) official censuses 1882-1907 (11,267; 13,485; 15,624) and Abu-Lughod (1965) 1947 census (20k-25k bracket).

Kafr el-Zayat-Egypt.name: Kafr el-Zayat
Kafr el-Zayat-Egypt.evidence_basis: Rosetta-branch railway bridgehead (1856) and major cotton-ginning/soap-oil hub with Greek merchant community; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947 (Abu-Lughod 1965: 20k-25k bracket in 1947).

Belqas-Egypt.name: Belqas
Belqas-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Gharbiya/Dakahlia rice-cultivating markaz town; 1846 registers and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Samanud-Egypt.name: Samanud
Samanud-Egypt.evidence_basis: Damietta-branch pottery and textile town in Gharbiya; Description de l'Egypte, 1907 census (EB11: 14,408), and 1882-1947 official censuses.

Maadi-Egypt.name: Maadi
Maadi-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1904 by Delta Land and Investment Company as planned garden suburb on the Cairo-Helwan railway; 1907-1947 census sub-district estimates and WWII Allied camp expansion.

El-Sinbillawayn-Egypt.name: El-Sinbillawayn
El-Sinbillawayn-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern Dakahlia cotton and grain railway markaz center between Zagazig and Mansoura; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Esna-Egypt.name: Esna
Esna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Upper Egypt weaving/barrage town (Esna Barrage built 1906-1909 temporarily boosting 1907 census to 19,103 in EB11); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Dairut-Egypt.name: Dairut
Dairut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Asyut irrigation regulator town (Dairut Regulator built 1871 on Ibrahimiya Canal and Bahr Yusuf); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Edfu-Egypt.name: Edfu
Edfu-Egypt.evidence_basis: Aswan-province agricultural markaz seat; 1907 census (EB11: 19,262 incl. contiguous rural hamlets) and 1882-1947 Egyptian census returns.

Abu Tig-Egypt.name: Abu Tig
Abu Tig-Egypt.evidence_basis: Asyut-province river grain and cattle market town; Description de l'Egypte and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Beni Mazar-Egypt.name: Beni Mazar
Beni Mazar-Egypt.evidence_basis: Minya-province agricultural markaz seat on the Ibrahimiya Canal and rail corridor; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Manzala-Egypt.name: El-Manzala
El-Manzala-Egypt.evidence_basis: Eastern Dakahlia fishing and rice-milling town on Lake Manzala; Description de l'Egypte and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Fuwa-Egypt.name: Fuwa
Fuwa-Egypt.evidence_basis: Rosetta-branch tarbush/textile manufacturing town (Muhammad Ali fez factory 1824); Description de l'Egypte, 1907 census (EB11: 14,515), and 1882-1947 censuses.

Qus-Egypt.name: Qus
Qus-Egypt.evidence_basis: Medieval Upper Egyptian entrepot surviving as Qena-province markaz town; Description de l'Egypte, official censuses 1882-1947, and Abu-Lughod (1965).

Edku-Egypt.name: Edku
Edku-Egypt.evidence_basis: Beheira coastal fishing, weaving, and date-palm town on Lake Edku; Description de l'Egypte and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Biba-Egypt.name: Biba
Biba-Egypt.evidence_basis: Beni Suef cotton and grain markaz seat; 1846 provincial census and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Tema-Egypt.name: Tema
Tema-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Sohag/Girga agricultural markaz town on Upper Egypt rail line; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Kom Ombo-Egypt.name: Kom Ombo
Kom Ombo-Egypt.evidence_basis: Small village transformed after 1904 Wadi Kom Ombo Company land-reclamation and 1912 sugar-factory construction; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Samalut-Egypt.name: Samalut
Samalut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Minya-province market and limestone-quarrying markaz town; 1846 registers and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Abu Qurqas-Egypt.name: Abu Qurqas
Abu Qurqas-Egypt.evidence_basis: Middle Egypt sugarcane-crushing center (large Societe des Sucreries factory built 1869); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Hawamdiya-Egypt.name: El-Hawamdiya
El-Hawamdiya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Giza-province Nile town transformed after 1881 construction of Egypt's premier sugar refinery (Societe Generale des Sucreries et de la Raffinerie d'Egypte); 1882-1947 Giza returns.

Armant-Egypt.name: Armant
Armant-Egypt.evidence_basis: Major Upper Egyptian sugarcane plantation and Societe des Sucreries refinery center (1869) south of Luxor; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Minya el-Qamh-Egypt.name: Minya el-Qamh
Minya el-Qamh-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southwestern Sharqia grain and cotton markaz seat on Banha-Zagazig rail line; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Qusiya-Egypt.name: El-Qusiya
El-Qusiya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Asyut-province agrarian and Coptic pilgrimage town near Deir el-Muharraq; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Nag Hammadi-Egypt.name: Nag Hammadi
Nag Hammadi-Egypt.evidence_basis: Qena-province sugar-refining and Nile rail-bridge town (Societe des Sucreries mill 1896; Nag Hammadi Barrage completed 1930); official censuses 1882-1947.

Abu Kabir-Egypt.name: Abu Kabir
Abu Kabir-Egypt.evidence_basis: Sharqia railway junction (Zagazig-Mansoura-Salhiya lines) and cotton-market town; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Shirbin-Egypt.name: Shirbin
Shirbin-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Dakahlia markaz town on the Damietta branch and Mansoura-Damietta railway; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Balyana-Egypt.name: El-Balyana
El-Balyana-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern Sohag/Girga Nile town and gateway to Abydos; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Dishna-Egypt.name: Dishna
Dishna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Qena-province sugarcane and grain markaz seat; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Qanater el-Khayriya-Egypt.name: El-Qanater el-Khayriya
El-Qanater el-Khayriya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1843 at the apex of the Nile Delta around Muhammad Ali's Delta Barrages (rebuilt 1884-1890 and 1939); 1846 and 1882-1947 Qalyubiya census returns.

Ibshaway-Egypt.name: Ibshaway
Ibshaway-Egypt.evidence_basis: Western Faiyum agricultural markaz town on light railway; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Arish-Egypt.name: El-Arish
El-Arish-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northern Sinai garrison and administrative capital; 1907 census (EB11: 5,897), WWI wartime evacuation dip (1917), 1937 census (9,706), and 1947-1952 growth incl. 1948 refugees.

El-Wasta-Egypt.name: El-Wasta
El-Wasta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Railway junction connecting Upper Egypt trunk line to the Faiyum branch (1874); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Naqada-Egypt.name: Naqada
Naqada-Egypt.evidence_basis: Historic west-bank Coptic and handloom-weaving town opposite Qus; Description de l'Egypte and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Badrashein-Egypt.name: El-Badrashein
El-Badrashein-Egypt.evidence_basis: Giza-province markaz center and rail station adjacent to ancient Memphis and Saqqara; 1846 and 1882-1947 Giza census returns.

Al-Shiyâkha 1-Egypt.name: Al-Shiyâkha 1
other_names: الشياخة الثانية (وتشمل المجاورات من رقم ? الي رقم ??)
الشياخة الثالثة (وتشمل المجاورات من رقم 20 الي رقم 52)

Kafrat Nassâr wa-Funduq Mînâ Haws (& Hot.name: Kafrat Nassâr wa-Funduq Mînâ Haws (& Hotel Mena House

Birket el-Sab-Egypt.name: Birket el-Sab
Birket el-Sab-Egypt.evidence_basis: Menufia railway bridgehead across Bahr Shibin on the main Cairo-Alexandria line (1856); official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Atfih-Egypt.name: Atfih
Atfih-Egypt.evidence_basis: Former Ottoman provincial capital of Atfihiya on east bank of Nile; Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882-1947 Giza returns.

El-Delengat-Egypt.name: El-Delengat
El-Delengat-Egypt.evidence_basis: Western Beheira markaz center on the western Delta reclamation margin; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Hosh Isa-Egypt.name: Hosh Isa
Hosh Isa-Egypt.evidence_basis: Western Beheira pastoral-agrarian market town between Damanhur and Maryut; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Daraw-Egypt.name: Daraw
Daraw-Egypt.evidence_basis: Traditional Ababda/Sudan camel-caravan market town north of Aswan; Burckhardt (1819), 1846 registers, and official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Abu Qir-Egypt.name: Abu Qir
Abu Qir-Egypt.evidence_basis: Coastal fishing and military headland east of Alexandria (linked by Ramleh-Abu Qir railway; RAF base from 1916); 1882-1947 Alexandria/Beheira returns.

Fayed-Egypt.name: Fayed
Fayed-Egypt.evidence_basis: Great Bitter Lake settlement on Ismailia-Suez railway and freshwater canal, expanded sharply as headquarters of British Middle East Land Forces (1946-1952); Canal Zone census returns.

Abu Tisht-Egypt.name: Abu Tisht
Abu Tisht-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northwestern Qena agricultural town along the Nile bend railway; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

El-Husseiniya-Egypt.name: El-Husseiniya
El-Husseiniya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northeastern Sharqia marsh-reclamation markaz center near ancient Tanis; official Egyptian censuses 1882-1947.

Baltim-Egypt.name: Baltim
Baltim-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northernmost Delta coast fishing and date-palm markaz town on Lake Burullus; 1846 and 1882-1947 Gharbiya census returns.

El-Salhiya-Egypt.name: El-Salhiya
El-Salhiya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Eastern Delta frontier town on the ancient Syria-Sinai caravan road; Description de l'Egypte, 1907 census (EB11: 6,100), and 1882-1947 Sharqia returns.

El-Qantara-Egypt.name: El-Qantara
El-Qantara-Egypt.evidence_basis: Established 1861 as Suez Canal caravan ferry station and expanded into major WWI Sinai-Palestine railway base (1916-1918); 1882-1947 Canal Zone census returns.

Marsa Matruh-Egypt.name: Marsa Matruh
Marsa Matruh-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northwestern Mediterranean port and Western Frontier District capital (1917); linked by railway to Alexandria in 1936 and expanded during WWII Western Desert campaigns (1927-1947 censuses).

Hurghada-Egypt.name: Hurghada
Hurghada-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1905 as Red Sea fishing outpost and Anglo-Egyptian Oilfields settlement (oil struck 1913); 1917-1947 Red Sea Frontier District census returns.

Quseir-Egypt.name: Quseir
Quseir-Egypt.evidence_basis: Ottoman/Khedival Red Sea grain/Hajj port declining after Suez Canal opening (1907 census EB11: 794), then reviving after 1911 Italian Red Sea Phosphate Company mining operations.

Port Fuad-Egypt.name: Port Fuad
Port Fuad-Egypt.evidence_basis: Inaugurated December 1926 by King Fuad I as Suez Canal Company residential town on the Sinai bank opposite Port Said; 1927-1947 Canal Governorate returns.

Ras Gharib-Egypt.name: Ras Gharib
Ras Gharib-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded April 1938 as Anglo-Egyptian Oilfields company town following discovery of Egypt's largest pre-1952 oilfield; 1947 Red Sea Governorate census.

Mut-Egypt.name: Mut
Mut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Administrative capital of Dakhla Oasis (oasis total 17,090 in 1897 and 18,368 in 1907, EB11 & Kato/Iwasaki); official Egyptian censuses 1897-1947.

Zahrâ', al- (Ahmâdiyyat al-Fitûh-Egypt.name: Zahrâ', al- (Ahmâdiyyat al-Fitûh
other_names: الزهراء (كفر ميت أبو غالب سا بقا)

Safaga-Egypt.name: Safaga
Safaga-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1911 by the Egyptian Phosphate Company as deepwater mineral-export port and rail terminus from Umm el-Huwaytat mines; 1917-1947 Red Sea District returns.

Rafah-Egypt.name: Rafah
Rafah-Egypt.evidence_basis: Sinai-Palestine border post demarcated in 1906 Taba-Rafah boundary agreement and WWI railway station; 1907-1947 Sinai Governorate census returns.

Qasr el-Dakhla-Egypt.name: Qasr el-Dakhla
Qasr el-Dakhla-Egypt.evidence_basis: Historic Islamic capital and largest mudbrick walled town of Dakhla Oasis; Beadnell (1901 Dakhla Oasis), 1907 Census of Egypt, and Kato & Iwasaki 1897-1947 Dakhla demographic series.

Siwa-Egypt.name: Siwa
Siwa-Egypt.evidence_basis: Annexed by Muhammad Ali in 1820; 1907 official census (EB11: 3,884), slight 1917 dip after Senussi conflict, and 1927-1947 Western Desert oasis returns.

Aniba-Egypt.name: Aniba
Aniba-Egypt.evidence_basis: Lower Nubian district center elevated to administrative capital of Egyptian Nubia in 1933 after the second raising of the Aswan Low Dam inundated El-Derr; 1882-1947 Aswan returns.

El-Bawiti-Egypt.name: El-Bawiti
El-Bawiti-Egypt.evidence_basis: Capital of Bahariya Oasis (total oasis ~6,000 in 1907 census; Ball & Beadnell 1903 Baharia Oasis); 1897-1947 Minya/Western Desert census returns.

Wadi el-Natrun-Egypt.name: Wadi el-Natrun
Wadi el-Natrun-Egypt.evidence_basis: Natron-extraction depression and Coptic monastic valley; expanded around Bir Hooker salt/soda company town and narrow-gauge railway (1899 Egyptian Salt and Soda Company).

El-Dabaa-Egypt.name: El-Dabaa
El-Dabaa-Egypt.evidence_basis: Mediterranean coastal station between Alexandria and Marsa Matruh (Maryut railway terminus 1909-1935; WWII airfield); 1907-1947 Western Desert returns.

Abu Zenima-Egypt.name: Abu Zenima
Abu Zenima-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 1913 by Sinai Mining Company as Gulf of Suez manganese-ore export port linked by railway to Umm Bogma mines; 1917-1947 Sinai returns.

Korosko-Egypt.name: Korosko
Korosko-Egypt.evidence_basis: Lower Nubian Nile-to-Abu Hamed caravan and Anglo-Egyptian military station (1882-1898), declining sharply after the 1899 Sudan Railway bypassed it (1907-1947 Aswan Nubia returns).

El-Derr-Egypt.name: El-Derr
El-Derr-Egypt.evidence_basis: Traditional administrative capital of Egyptian Lower Nubia (markaz al-Derr until 1933); Burckhardt (1819), 1882-1947 Aswan Nubia returns showing post-1933 reservoir displacement.

El-Tor-Egypt.name: El-Tor
El-Tor-Egypt.evidence_basis: South Sinai Red Sea port and major international Hajj maritime quarantine station (expanded 1877-1900); 1882-1947 Sinai census and Sanitary Board records.

Sheikh Zuweid-Egypt.name: Sheikh Zuweid
Sheikh Zuweid-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northeastern Sinai oasis village on the El-Arish-Rafah coastal road and WWI railway; 1907-1947 Sinai Governorate census returns.

Baris-Egypt.name: Baris
Baris-Egypt.evidence_basis: Principal southern oasis town of the Kharga depression on the Darb al-Arba'in route; Beadnell (1909), 1907 Census of Egypt, and 1917-1947 Southern Desert returns.

Sallum-Egypt.name: Sallum
Sallum-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northwestern border port on the Libyan frontier (formally garrisoned by Egypt in 1911 during Italo-Turkish War); 1917-1947 Western Desert Frontier returns.

El-Alamein-Egypt.name: El-Alamein
El-Alamein-Egypt.evidence_basis: Coastal Maryut railway whistle-stop and Bedouin hamlet devastated during the 1942 Battles of El-Alamein; 1907-1947 Western Desert Frontier returns.

El-Milga-Egypt.name: El-Milga
El-Milga-Egypt.evidence_basis: High-Sinai Gebeliya Bedouin village settlement in Wadi el-Raha; Burckhardt (1822) and 1907-1947 Sinai Frontier District returns.

Qasr el-Farafra-Egypt.name: Qasr el-Farafra
Qasr el-Farafra-Egypt.evidence_basis: Sole permanent walled settlement of Farafra Oasis; Beadnell (1901 Farafra Oasis), 1897-1907 official census (542 to 632), and 1917-1947 Western Desert returns.

Nekhel-Egypt.name: Nekhel
Nekhel-Egypt.evidence_basis: Central Sinai fortress on the Darb al-Hajj pilgrim road and pre-WWI Sinai administrative headquarters until wrecked in 1915-1917; Sinai Frontier District returns.
